title: Palindrome Partitioning
statement: Split the string into consecutive pieces so that every piece is a palindrome. Return all possible partitions, in any order. The string has at least one character.

hints.1_question: A partition is a sequence of cut positions. At each start position, which prefixes are allowed as the next piece?
hints.2_nudge: Try every prefix s[start:end]; if it is a palindrome, take it and recurse on the rest; otherwise skip it.
hints.3_big_hint: bt(start): if start == len(s) record a copy; for end in start+1..len(s): sub = s[start:end]; if sub == sub[::-1]: append, bt(end), pop.

known_bugs.name: only splits into single characters
known_bugs.followup: In 'aab' can 'aa' stay together as one palindromic piece?

known_bugs.name: never checks that pieces are palindromes
known_bugs.followup: For 'abc', is 'ab' a palindrome? Where do you check?

known_bugs.name: stores the live list instead of a copy
known_bugs.followup: After the search ends, what do the lists in `res` contain?

followups: How can you precompute which substrings are palindromes (DP) to speed up the checks?
How many partitions can a string of n equal letters have?
